nodes.description:
Anti-CD19 depletion, which reaches a broader span of the B-cell lineage than anti-CD20 does - including the plasmablasts this entry curates as the type 1 driver. That is the mechanistic argument for preferring it over rituximab, and it is now supported by the only randomised controlled evidence in this disease area.
Two limits on how far this record should be read. The trial enrolled IgG4-related disease rather than autoimmune pancreatitis specifically, so it applies to type 1 and to nothing else here. And severe adverse events, particularly infections and lymphopenia, were more frequent on treatment.

The evidence is a review describing it as promising, not a trial. Type 2 is rare enough that no controlled evidence exists, which is the same constraint that makes its natural history a knowledge gap in this entry.

nodes.description:
The current effector paradigm. An unconventional CD4-positive cytotoxic T-cell population bearing SLAMF7 is oligoclonally expanded in patients, is found as the same dominant clones in blood and in affected tissue, and contracts on glucocorticoid-induced remission. It is thought to be sustained by continuous antigen presentation from the plasmablast compartment, which makes the B-cell and T-cell arms mutually reinforcing rather than sequential.
This supersedes the type 2 helper T cell account that the older literature gives, and the entry keeps both: the Th2 subsets are named on the node above because they are what the cited reviews describe, and this node is where the cell that is currently thought to do the damage lives.

nodes.description:
The type 3 lesion, and mechanistically a third disease under one name. Checkpoint inhibitors remove the restraint on T-cell activation, and the resulting pancreatic injury is acinar-centric T-cell infiltration that evolves from CD4-predominant to CD8-predominant over time.
It is a separate root node with no edge to the other two arms, for the same reason the type 1 and type 2 triggers have no edge between them: nothing in the cited literature connects them mechanistically. What it shares with them is that it damages the pancreas, and even the shared endpoint is different - most type 3 disease presents as asymptomatic lipase elevation rather than as a mass, so it does not converge on the tumefactive node the other two arms meet at.

nodes.description:
Oral corticosteroids, typically four weeks followed by a taper, are the initial treatment of both type 1 and type 2. The response is the defining therapeutic fact about this disease and is also diagnostic in practice, since a steroid-responsive pancreatic mass is very unlikely to be adenocarcinoma.
Note that it works in both subtypes despite the two having different mechanisms. That is not a paradox - corticosteroids suppress both lymphoplasmacytic and neutrophilic inflammation - but it does mean treatment response cannot be used as evidence that the two share a pathogenesis.

Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltration of the pancreas, rich in IgG4-positive plasma cells, with obliterative venulitis. This is the cellular half of the type 1 tissue lesion and it is what the diagnostic criteria count.
The role of IgG4 itself is the interesting uncertainty. It is the diagnostic marker of the disease and may not be the agent of it: other IgG subclasses have been proposed as the mediators, with IgG4 representing a response that dampens excessive inflammation rather than causing it.

nodes.description:
The innate ignition step, and the most upstream node in the type 1 arm. Neutrophil extracellular traps in the inflamed pancreas activate plasmacytoid dendritic cells to produce interferon-alpha, and that interferon environment is what drives B cells toward IgG4 rather than IgG1 class switching.
This node carries the strongest causal evidence in the entry, and it is the only interventional evidence: in the mouse model, depleting pDCs or blocking interferon-alpha prevents the disease. Everything downstream of here is observational in humans. It is placed upstream of the adaptive node because it supplies the signal that shapes the adaptive response rather than following from it.

Lymphoplasmacytic inflammation of and around the small veins, obliterating their lumen. The third member of the type 1 histologic triad, and until this round the only one of the three this entry named in prose without curating.
It is curated as its own node for the same reason the infiltration and fibrosis nodes are separate: the three are separately assessed by the diagnostic criteria, and one of them discriminates between subtypes. Checkpoint-inhibitor pancreatitis does not produce it, so its absence is informative rather than merely unmeasured.

nodes.description:
The standard experimental model of the disease. Repeated intraperitoneal polyinosinic-polycytidylic acid in autoimmune-prone MRL/Mp mice produces pancreatic immune cell infiltration, fibrosis and destruction of pancreatic architecture, with extrapancreatic involvement and raised serum autoantibodies.
It is worth being explicit about what kind of model this is. There is no genetic lesion and no antigen - the disease is induced by a generic innate-immune stimulus in a strain that is already predisposed to autoimmunity. So the model reproduces the tissue outcome of the disease without reproducing anything about its cause, and it cannot be used to argue for a particular trigger.

nodes.description:
B-cell depletion for relapsing type 1 disease. It is mechanistically the most targeted therapy available here, because it removes the compartment whose oligoclonal expansion characterises the disease, and it is used precisely where the disease behaviour - relapse - reflects that ongoing B-cell response.
Relapse is largely a type 1 problem. It is common in type 1 and relatively uncommon in type 2, which is why this treatment belongs to one subtype rather than to the entry as a whole.

nodes.description:
Cartwheel or storiform fibrosis, the fibrotic response to the lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate and the component that turns an inflammatory lesion into a mass.
Split from the infiltration node in review. The two were bundled, and the bundling was doing real damage: the poly(I:C) mouse model speaks to this node and cannot in principle speak to the one above, because mice have no IgG4 subclass. With one node that had to be a single PARTIALLY_RECAPITULATES link carrying an apologetic limitations string covering both halves. With two, each node gets the claim it deserves - a partial match here, because the model reports fibrosis and architectural destruction rather than the storiform pattern specifically, and a FAILS_TO_RECAPITULATE against the node above, because the absence there is structural rather than unmeasured.
An earlier version of this paragraph said the split would yield "a clean RECAPITULATES here". It does not, and the link is correctly PARTIALLY_RECAPITULATES. The sentence was written in one review round describing an intended structure, the structure landed differently in the next, and the prose was not re-read against it. That is the same defect this entry corrects twice in its own notes, so it is recorded rather than quietly overwritten.

Both the plasma-cell and fibrotic lesion and the neutrophilic duct lesion expand the gland into a mass that is radiologically indistinguishable from pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The single most consequential fact about this disease is that it is a steroid-responsive mimic of a cancer that is treated by resection.

nodes.description: The immune driver of type 1 disease. Several T-cell subsets are implicated - type 2 helper T cells, regulatory T cells and T follicular helper 2 cells - alongside an oligoclonal expansion of plasmablasts whose dominant clones differ between patients and re-emerge as distinct clones at relapse. The clonality is the part that matters mechanistically: it is antigen-driven selection rather than a polyclonal inflammatory response, and it is what makes B-cell depletion a rational therapy.

nodes.description: The lesion of type 2, and mechanistically a different disease from type 1. Neutrophils infiltrate the lumen and epithelium of small and medium pancreatic ducts, destroying ductal architecture - the granulocytic epithelial lesion. Duct epithelium and infiltrating T lymphocytes both express CXCL8 (IL-8), which is the proposed recruitment signal for the neutrophilic inflammation that defines this subtype.
